## Harper's transliteration, line by line (col · line · text)
Raised text in braces: {b}, {ilu} = the divine determinative (write it {d} with the AN sign, role det), {amêlu} = the LÚ determinative, {kam}. Harper writes many logograms as the Akkadian word (eḳlam for A.ŠÀ) — the plate decides the sign. ḳ = q.

## Notes from the transcription (apparatus)

- Col. XXXIV: from §206 through §221 Harper's running line numerals are one higher than the ranges in his own §-headings (text gives the column 96 lines, headings imply 95). The source follows the running numerals; check the column length against the autograph plate before citing by line.
- Col. XXXVIII 31–36: not in Harper — §262 breaks off after line 30 in a row of dots (damage on the stele) and §263 begins at 37.
- Words split across Harper's page turns were joined: XVII 60 tamka-rum, XIX 47 i-du-uk-ku, XXIX 73, XXX 65 iš-ru-ḳu-ši-im, XLII 56, XLIV 35.
- line XXIX 73: the page ends mid-word with 'i-nu-'; the rest of the word and lines 74–XXX 9 are on Cornell p. 84 (not in this batch). Join with the hyphen kept when merging.
- XXX 65: only 'iš-' is printed on this page; the word continues at the top of Cornell p. 86 as 'ru-ḳu-ši-im' (full word iš-ru-ḳu-ši-im). Kept split across files, not duplicated.
- XXIX 78: stray mark after 'warad' at line end; ignored. XXIX 85 and XXX 55: capitals broken across printed lines (MAŠ. / EN.KAK, NU.MU. / SU) joined without space.
- XXX 43 'šu-a-ti': the i of ti has a mark under it that may be a dot (ṭị?) — read as plain ti, likely a print speck.
- XXX 44 'i-pa-ak-ki-du-ma' and XXX 48 'ṣi-iḫ-ḫi-ru-tim': the hyphens ki-du and ḫi-ru look like a colon/odd dash in the print; read as ordinary hyphens.
- XXX 53 'ša-a-a-ma-nu-um': small mark above the second ma; read as print noise.
- XXX 59 'ŠA.GA. a-na' — period after GA printed, copied.
- XXX 61 '{b}ŠAL(?)' raised b before ŠAL printed here (the parallel § 179 on the next page has no raised b).
- carry XXX 65: page opens with 'ru-ḳu-ši-im', the tail of 'iš-' printed at the end of Cornell p. 84 (full word iš-ru-ḳu-ši-im); kept split across the two files, not duplicated.
- XXX 75 'la u-ša-am-zi-ši': the l of 'la' is oddly formed (looks like a dotted/broken l); read as la.
- XXX 84 'ŠE.BA NI.BA {b}u ŠIG.BA': ŠIG. / BA broken across printed lines, joined; small mark before BA at line start ignored.

- XXX 89 'ki-ma': speck before ki ignored. XXX 68, 70, 71, 72: specks near numerals ignored.
- XXXI 18 'ab-lu-za': a faint colon-like speck before the word ignored.

- XXXI 21 and XXXI 46 'zinništi': a dot appears under the second n in XXXI 21 (zinṇišti?) — read as print speck; XXXI 46 is clean.

- XXXI 54 'iš-te-en': speck below/after te ignored; speck under 54 ignored.

## Signs already in the shared sign glossary (signs-cuneiform.json) — key: values

- AN: an, diĝir (as det. {d}), Akkadian: Anum (the sky-god, the bare sign), ilum “god”
- NAM: Akkadian: nam
- LUGAL: Akkadian value šarrum “king”
- TA: ta
- E: e, e₃, è, Akkadian: e
- NE: ne, de₃, bil, dè — in A.GA.NE (Agade), bí
- A: Akkadian: a, A.ŠÀ = eqlum “field”, plural marker with ḪI (Harper reads ḪI+A as ZUN, §35)
- BA: Akkadian: ba
- NUN: nun, eridu (with KI), Akkadian: nun
- KI: ki 'place/earth', Akkadian: ki, qi₂; also the syllable ki in words
- LU: Akkadian: lu, second sign of SIPA “shepherd”, as logogram UDU — “sheep”, Akkadian immerum, lū “or; let …”, ṣēnum “sheep,
- LA: Akkadian: la
- GAR: ĝar, gar, qar — in qar-ra-dum “warrior”, GAR/NINDA — “bread, portion”, ŠA.GA (Harper) / NÍG.GA = makkūrum “property” (§6
- MU: Akkadian: mu, MU = šattum “year”: MU III{kam} “the third year” (§30)
- NI: ni, ì, Akkadian: ni, li₂, ì
- AK: ak, aĝ₂, aq
- IB: Akkadian: ib, ip, the god Uraš of Dilbat ({d}IB)
- BI: Akkadian: bi, bé, pi₂
- RU: ru, šub, Akkadian: ru
- DU: du, ĝen, gub, rá, DU — “to go, stand”
- EN: Akkadian: en; EN = bēlum “lord”; EN.LÍL = the god Enlil
- ME: Akkadian: me
- LU2: lù, lú, determinative before persons: {amēlu}agram “hireling” (§26, §33)
- NA: Akkadian: na
- GAL: GAL — “great”; GAL.GAL “the great (gods)”; GAL.BÚR = ušumgallum “dragon”; gál
- TUR: dumu, tur, as DUMU — “son”, Akkadian mārum, DUMU — mār “son”, DUMU+ti = mārtum “daughter” (§38–39)
- ZI: Akkadian: ṣi, ṣe
- PA: pa, sib (PA.LU), Akkadian: pa, PA.LU = SIPA “shepherd” (rēʾûm); PA.AL = šabra (in Mashkan-shabri), PA.PA — the captain (
- RA: Akkadian: ra
- URU: uru, eri, iri, Akkadian: ri₂ (in da-ri₂-tam “everlasting”), unu — Harper’s UNU.KI (Uruk) and UD.UNU.KI (Larsa); modern e
- ESZ: eš
- A2: Akkadian: id, it (ni-bi-it)
- IGI: igi, lim (in Alulim), Akkadian: ši; Sumerian igi “eye”
- EZENxBAD: in Dur-ilu{ki} (Der), “Fortress of the god”
- DUB: dub
- NAGAR: nagar, tibira, agru “hired man” — Harper’s own sign-list value; modern editions read the word as ḪUN.GÁ (§26, §33)
- ESH2: šè, šú
- UD: ud, u₄, Akkadian: ud, ut, tam; as logogram UTU = Šamaš, the sun-god, babbar — É.BABBAR.RA (Ebabbar, “Shining House”), ūm
- KIB: kib — the sign of UD.KIB.NUN (Sippar) and the Euphrates
- SU: su, SU — “flesh”
- KUR: kur, land, mountain, KUR — “mountain, land”; É.KUR = Ekur, Enlil’s temple, mat, šad
- DUR2: dúr, tuš
- MA: Akkadian: ma
- UR2: úr
- EGIR: egir
- DISH: 1 — I MA.NA “one mina” (§24)
- U: the numeral 10: adi 10-šu “tenfold” (§8)
- GESH2: 60
- GESHU: 600
- SHAR2: 3,600
- SHARU: 36,000
- SHARGAL: 216,000
- I: i
- BAD: be, bad, bat, til
- EL: el
- SHA: ša
- U3: ù (u₃) — the conjunction “and”
- IR: ir, er
- DIM: tim, dim, ṭim
- AD: ad, at, aṭ
- KALAM: KALAM — Sumerian “land”, read mātum in Akkadian, un
- AMAR: AMAR — “calf”; with UTU spells Marduk (AMAR.UTU, “calf of the Sun”)
- RI: ri, re, tal
- ESH: eš, 30 — three Winkelhaken, the numeral 30: adi 30-šu “thirtyfold” (§8)
- TI: ti, ṭi, TI — “arrow”, also “life” (Sumerian ti(l))
- IM: im, em, IM — also “clay, storm”, as logogram: {d}IM = Adad, the storm-god; {uru}IM{ki} = Karkar
- KISH: KIŠ — read kiššat “all, totality” in Akkadian (Harper’s sign list: ner, kiš, šēpu, kiššatu), ner (Harper) — {uru}NER.KI 
- TAG: šum, tag, tak, šum — in šum-ma “if”, the word that opens every law
- IN: in
- GI4: gi₄, ge₄
- U2: u₂ — the commonest writing of vowel u in Old Babylonian, Sumerian ú “plant”
- SAR: šar, SAR — Sumerian “garden / to write”, {giš}SAR (KIRI₆) = kirûm “orchard” (§27 on)
- SHU: šu, ŠU — “hand”, ŠU.ḪA = bāʾirum “fisher” (§26–41)
- KA2: KA₂ — “gate”; opens KA₂.DINGIR.RA “Babylon”, Bāb-ilim “gate of the god”, KÁ.GAL = abullum, the city gate (§15)
- TE: te, ṭe₄
- LI: li, le
- DA: da, ṭa
- HA: ḫa, ḪA — “fish”, second sign of ŠU.ḪA = bāʾirum “fisher”
- AM: am, AM — “wild bull” (GUD×KUR)
- AH: aḫ, eḫ, iḫ, uḫ, a’ — carries the glottal stop (ʾ) in words like na-a’-dam
- DAM: dam, DAM — “spouse”, DAM.GÀR = tamkārum “merchant” (§40), dam — “spouse”
- IA: ia (i+a ligature) — the sound y
- GA: ga, qa₂
- UL: ul
- HU: ḫu, MUŠEN — “bird” (as det.)
- KAL: dan — in dannum “strong”, kal, KAL — “mighty, precious”, LAMMA — the lamassu guardian spirit, dan — “strong”
- SAG: SAG — “head”; SAG.GI₆ “the black-headed” = mankind, sag
- MI: mi, gi₆ / gig₂ — “black, night”; second sign of SAG.GI₆
- PI: wa, wi, wu, pi — one sign for all the w-syllables
- TU: tu, ṭu₂
- UB: ub, up
- BU: bu, pu
- KU: ku, qu₂, KU — “to lie down”
- UR: ur, UR — “dog”
- NU: nu, Sumerian nu “not”, NU.TUR — the lieutenant (modern: laputtûm) §33–34
- UM: um
- KID: lil₂ — in {d}EN.LÍL “Enlil”, kid
- ISH: iš, Akkadian: iš, uš₅
- IGIGUNU: ši — the IGI sign with extra strokes (gunû); Harper writes ši(g), sig₇
- LUH: luḫ; ŠU.LUḪ = šuluḫḫu “purification-rites”
- ZU: zu, ZU — “to know”; in É.ZU.AB (E-abzu) and EN.ZU (Sin)
- AB: ab, ap, AB — “window”; in É.ZU.AB and ŠEŠ.AB (Ur)
- GISH: iz, is, iṣ, GIŠ — “wood, tree”; GIŠ.DAR = Ištar (old writing)
- IL2: íl — in É.SAG.ÍL.LA (Esagila)
- IL: il
- KUL: NUMUN — “seed”; Akkadian zērum (Harper: zêr, ZIR)
- SHESH: ŠEŠ — “brother”; opens ŠEŠ.AB (Ur)
- USH: uš, nit (Harper, in nit-ra-ru-šu), second sign of AGA₃.ÚS = rēdûm “soldier”, uš, nit
- GUM: qum, kum
- BIL: bil — the NE sign with extra strokes; in ba-bil “bringer”
- GAN: gan, ḫé — in ḪÉ.GÁL ḫegallum “abundance”; also the syllable in Da-gan
- SUHUSH: SUḪUŠ — “foundation”, Akkadian išdum (Harper: išid)
- GU: gu, {giš}GU.ZA = kussûm “chair, seat of office” (§5)
- MUSH3: {d}INANNA — the goddess Ishtar (Harper reads Nanâ), muš₃
- TUG2: dul₃ — in AN.DUL₃ ṣalūlum “protective canopy”, túg — “cloth, garment”
- TUM: tum, dum
- BUR2: búr — GAL.BÚR = ušumgallum, the dragon
- LUM: lum
- GA2: ma₃/mal — in {d}za-ma₃-ma₃ (Zamama) and MAL.KA.A (Malka/Malgium)
- HAR: ḫar/ḫur — in ḪAR.SAG.KALAM.MA (Hursag-kalama, “Mountain of the Land”)
- KISAL: KISAL — “courtyard”, Akkadian kisallum
- GU2: gú/tig — opens TIG.GAB.A (Cutha)
- GABA: gab — in TIG.GAB.A (Cutha), GABA — “breast”; modern editions read du₈ here
- SHID: šid — Harper’s ŠID.LAM (the Meslam) and É.MIŠ.MIŠ (Emishmish), modern reading: mes
- KA: KA — “mouth”; ina pī mātim “in the mouth of the land”, ka (syllable)
- AR: ar — the AR sign (IGI+RI)
- GIR2: gír, kir — in kir-bu-um (qerbum “within”); opens GIR.SU (Girsu)
- SHIR: šir — opens ŠIR.PUR.LA (Lagash)
- BUR: bur, pur — in ŠIR.PUR.LA (Lagash)
- NIN: NIN — “lady/lord”; in NIN.TU (Nintu) and NIN.A.ZU (Ninazu)
- DI: di, ṭi, DI — “judgment” (salīmum)
- GI: gi, GI — “reed”
- AL: al
- MASH: maš — in É.UL.MAŠ (Eulmash) and MAŠ.KAN (Mashkan-)
- GAN2: kan — in MAŠ.KAN.PA.AL (Mashkan-shabri), GAN₂ — “field”
- AZ: az — the lion-sign with ZA inside
- SI: si, SI — “horn”
- SA: sa
- SHE: še, ŠE — “barley, grain”
- IG: ig, ik, iq
- TAB: tab, TAB — “to double, twin”
- GAM: gam — in mu-gam-me-ir “who heaps up”
- DAR: dar/tár — GIŠ.DAR = Ištar (the old writing iš₈-tár; Harper: Anunit)
- NIM: nim, NIM — “high; Elam”
- LAM: lam — in ŠID.LAM, the Meslam temple
- ENGUR: with A before river-names: {íd}, the river-marker (A.ENGUR = ÍD), with {d}: the divine River (ÍD), judge of the ordeal i
- ZA: za, ṣa
- HI: ḫi, ḪI — “to mix”, with A: plural marker of LID.GUD(.ḪI.A), Harper’s ZUN (§35)
- AS: aš, dil — in DIL.BAT (Dilbat), the simplest sign: one horizontal wedge
- MAH: MAḪ — “exalted”; in É.GAL.MAḪ and É.MAḪ
- KAR: KAR (the TE sign with extra strokes) — karûm “grain-heap”, kar (syllable) — in iz-za-kar “he declared” (zakārum), karum 
- SAL: ṣal — in ṣal-tum (Harper’s “warrior of Dagan”), SAL/MUNUS — “woman”, §40: Harper reads SAL alone as aššatum “wife” (?); 
- E2: É — “house, temple”; opens every temple name, Akkadian bītum, É.GAL-lum = ekallum “palace” (§32)
- BAR: bar — in Bar-zi-ba (Borsippa)
- NINNU: 50 — É.50 = Eninnu, “House Fifty”, Ningirsu’s temple
- KU3: KÙ — “pure, precious”; KÙ.BABBAR = kaspum “silver”, KÙ.GI = ḫurāṣum “gold”, KÙ.BABBAR = kaspum “silver”: kaspi-šu, kaspi
- GUD: GU₄ — “ox”, Akkadian alpum
- ARAD: ARAD — “slave, servant”, Akkadian wardum
- ANSHE: ANŠE — “donkey”, Akkadian imērum
- SHUBUR: ŠAḪ (šubur) — “pig”, Akkadian šaḫûm
- MA2: MÁ — “boat”, Akkadian eleppum
- KAK: KAK/GAG — “peg, nail”; MAŠ.EN.KAK = muškēnum, the commoner
- MIN: 2; with U: the numeral 12 (adi 12-šu “twelvefold”), 2 — II GÍN “two shekels” (§17)
- IA5: 5 — adi 5-šu “up to five times over” (§12)
- SHESH6: 6 — ITI VI{kam} “the sixth month” (§13)
- ITI: ITI — “month”, Akkadian warḫum: the UD “day” sign with 30 inside — a month of days
- KAM: after a numeral, makes it an ordinal: VI{kam} “the sixth”
- GIN2: GÍN — “shekel”, Akkadian šiqlum: the basic weight of silver, about 8.3 g, aga₃ — first sign of AGA₃.ÚS, Harper’s rid ṣâb
- SHA3: A.ŠÀ = eqlum “field” — the fief-land of §§26–41, ŠÀ — “heart, interior”
- AB2: ÁB — “cow”; opens Harper’s LID.GUD.ZUN = liātum “cattle” (§35)
- ERIN2: ERIM — “troops”: ṣāb nisḫātim “struck-off troops” (§33)
- GAR3: second sign of DAM.GÀR = tamkārum “merchant” (§40)
- GUN: GUN — biltum “yield, tribute”: nāši biltim “the rent-payer” (§37–38)
- GUR: gur — in i-gur-ma “he hired” (§26)
- KASKAL: KASKAL — “road, campaign”: ḫarrān šarrim (§33); elsewhere spelled ḫar-ra-an
- THREE: 3 — MU III{kam} “the third year” (§30)
- TIM: tim — in ni-is-ḫa-tim, bi-il-tim, ni-ip-la-tim, dim
- MAR: mar — in i-mar-ra-ar “he shall harrow” (§44)
- UZ3: uz — in i-zu-uz-zu “they shall divide” (§46)
- BURU14: BURU₁₄ = ebūrum “harvest”: ina ebūrim “at harvest” (§47, §49); Harper’s sign list: ebûru
- HAL: ḫal — in u-ḫal-li-qu “he destroyed” (ḫalāqum, §53)
- U8: U₈ — “ewe”; U₈.UDU{ḫi.a} = ṣēnū “sheep and goats, the flock” (§57–58)
- NAGA: second sign of SÍN in AB.SÍN = absinnum “furrow, ploughland” (§62; the identification on Harper’s plate is uncertain)
- LACUNA: 
- UN: un — in iš-ku-un “he placed” (§76 gap text)
- ZIB: ṣib — in ṣib-tam “interest” (Nippur tablet, §91, §94); identification not checked on the plate
- NA4: NA₄ = abnum “stone; stone weight”: ina abnim rabītim “by the large stone” (§108); Harper’s sign list no. 97 (abnu)
- DIN: TIN — in ŠAL.GEŠ.TIN.NA, the tavern-keeper, and GEŠ.TIN.NA “wine” (§108–111); Harper’s sign list no. 178 (din, tin)
- LAL: LÁ — last sign of ŠÀ.GAN₂.LÁ = šamallûm “the merchant’s agent” (§100–107); Harper’s sign list no. 181 (lal)
- SHAM2: ŠÁM = šīmum “price”: ana šīm šikarim “for the price of beer” (§108); Harper’s sign list no. 83 (šîmu) draws the sign as 
- SIG: SIG = šipātum “wool” (§104): Harper’s glossary writes šipâtu [SIG]; the plate sign (a box with a long wedge) is matched 
- FIVEBAN2: 5 BAN₂ = 50 qa: Harper’s “L QA” (§111), the numeral 50 fused with the measure sign (his List of Numerals shows “50 KA” i
- THIRD: 1/3 — ⅓ MA.NA kaspim “a third of a mina of silver” (§114, §116): on the plate (XIX 24, 49) one sign, two uprights over a
- SILA3: SÌLA = qa, the measure of capacity (about a litre): Harper’s ḲA: V ḲA šeʾim “five qa of grain” (§121); the plate draws i
- TIR: tir — in tir-ḫa-tum “bride-price” (§138–139); Harper’s tir-ḫa-ti-ša; identification not checked on the plate
- SUR: ṣur — in iṣ-ṣur-ma “she guarded” (§133A); Harper’s ṣur; identification not checked on the plate
- KAB: kab — in u-kab-bil-ši-ma “he held her down” (§130); Harper’s kab; identification not checked on the plate
- ZUM: zum — in u-li-zum “she bore him” (§162, §167): ūlissum, the ssum spelled with one sign; Harper’s zum, as in la-ma-zum (l
- UG: ug — in ug-dar-ri-zu (uktarriṣṣu, §161), uk, uq — in iš-ru-uq (išruk, §165)
